to any spacetimes is associated a unique (up to isomorphsims) symmetric tensor $${C^*}$$-category with conjugates, and that to embeddings between spacetimes correspond morphisms between the corresponding categories.
the charged sectors of a locally covariant theory are covariant, that the global and local sectors are the same, and that the gauge group is independent of the spacetime.
the theory of superselection sectors is a theory of categories and that the gauge group of any spacetime is the automorphism group of the associated category.

a generalization of the concept of superselection sectors in locally covariant field theories.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
superselection sectors in quantum field theories with a short-distance asymptotic limit are described by net-cohomology, and that the corresponding sectors are sharply localizable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of superselection sectors of charged particles is a theory of categories, with a natural notion of morphisms, which is covariant with respect to embeddings of spacetimes.
the theory of charged sectors in a globally hyperbolic background is equivalent to the theory of sectors on a simply connected spacetime.
the local and global structure of charged sectors is described by a unique, up-to-equivalence and up-to- isomorphism, category of Hilbert spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
superselection sectors are a natural object of the framework of locally covariant quantum theories.
the notion of superselection sectors is not only a local property of the theory but it is a property of the theory in the whole spacetime.

the notion of charged sectors, which are usually introduced in the context of globally hyperbolic manifolds, is well-defined in the framework of locally covariant quantum fields theories, and that it has a well defined behaviour with respect to embeddings between globally hyperbolic manifold.
